Nov 13, 2026


## Kolibri Global Energy Announces 15% YTD Increase in Production and 43% YTD Increase in Net Revenues


THOUSAND OAKS, Calif. –


All amounts are in U.S. Dollars unless otherwise indicated:


THIRD QUARTER 2026 HIGHLIGHTS


- Revenue, net of royalties was $18.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $15.0 million for the third quarter of 2025, which was an increase of 22% due to a 34% increase in average prices partially offset by a decrease in production of 9%


- Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was $3.6 million and Basic EPS was $0.10/share, which was the same as in the third quarter of 2025. Net income in the third quarter of 2026 included a $2.4 million unrealized loss on commodity contracts compared to a $0.5 million unrealized loss on commodity contracts in the third quarter of 2025. The higher revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was offset by a $1.0 million realized loss on commodity contracts and the unrealized loss mentioned above


- Adjusted EBITDA(1) was $13.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $11.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 20%. The increase was primarily due to the increase in revenue partially offset by the realized loss on commodity contracts in 2026


- Average production for the third quarter of 2026 was 3,867 BOEPD, a decrease of 9% compared to third quarter 2025 production of 4,254 BOEPD. The decrease in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to production on certain wells being temporarily shut in during the drilling and completion operations on the four new wells during the quarter along with normal production declines


- Production and operating expense per barrel averaged $8.39 per BOE in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $7.37 per BOE in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 14%. The increase was primarily due to higher severance taxes due to higher prices, workover costs on a non-operated well and higher chemical costs in 2026


- Average netback from operations(2) for the third quarter of 2026 was $43.48 per BOE, an increase of 41% from the prior year third quarter due to higher prices. Average netback including commodity contracts(2) for the third quarter of 2026 was $40.55 per BOE, an increase of 31% from the prior year third quarter


- In October 2026, the credit facility was redetermined with the same $75 million borrowing base. At September 30, 2026, the Company had $19.5 million of available borrowing capacity on its credit agreement.


(1)


Adjusted EBITDA is considered a non-GAAP measure. Refer to the section entitled “Non-GAAP Measures” of this earnings release.


(2)


Netback from operations and netback including commodity contracts are considered non-GAAP ratios. Refer to the section entitled “Non-GAAP Measures” of this earnings release.


KEI’s President and Chief Executive Officer, Wolf Regener commented:


“We are pleased with the Company’s performance for the first nine months of 2026 as we have continued to increase production, revenue and adjusted EBITDA from 2025 levels. For the third quarter of 2026, our revenue increased by 22% and our adjusted EBITDA increased by 20% compared to the third quarter of 2025 while production was down 9% due to temporarily shutting in some production during the drilling and completion operations on the four new wells and without bringing on any new wells since fourth quarter of 2025. As we recently announced, the Lovina 5-8-1HF well, which is our initial test of the False Caney bench, is performing very well with production averaging 636 BOEPD, which includes about 545 barrels of oil per day. Our 3 Clifton Mack wells are also performing well with recently announced combined production of about 1,911 BOEPD, which includes about 720 barrels of oil per day. All of these wells will contribute to our fourth quarter results which will further increase our production and cash flows at the end of 2026 and into 2027. After bringing on all of the new wells, our current production is approximately 5,700 BOE per day.”

Third Quarter 2026 versus Third Quarter 2025


Oil and gas gross revenues totaled $23.1 million in the third quarter of 2026 versus $18.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. Oil gross revenues totaled $20.9 million in the third quarter of 2026 versus $16.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. Oil revenues increased 27% as oil price increases of 33% were partially offset by oil production decreases of 5%. Natural gas revenues increased by 28% as natural gas prices increased 26% and production increased 1%. Natural gas liquids (NGLs) revenues decreased by 34% as NGL production decreased 32% and prices decreased by 2%.


Average third quarter 2026 production per day decreased 387 BOEPD or 9% from the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to production on certain wells being temporarily shut in during the drilling and completion operations on the four new wells during the quarter along with normal production declines.


Production and operating expenses were $2.5 million in both the third quarter of 2026 and 2025. Operating expense per barrel averaged $8.39 per BOE in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $7.37 per BOE in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 14%. The increase was primarily due to higher severance taxes due to higher prices, workover costs on a non-operated well and higher chemical costs in 2026.


Finance expense increased by $3.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 due to realized losses on commodity contracts of $1.0 million and an increase in unrealized losses on commodity contracts of $2.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.


FIRST NINE MONTHS 2026 HIGHLIGHTS


- Average production for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 4,412 BOEPD, an increase of 15% from the average production of 3,851 BOEPD in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to production on the wells that were drilled and completed in the fourth quarter of 2025


- Revenue, net of royalties was $60.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $42.1 million for the first nine months of 2025, which was an increase of 43%, as production increased by 15% and average prices increased by 24%


- Net income for the first nine months of 2026 was $16.1 million and Basic EPS was $0.45/share compared to net income of $12.2 million and Basic EPS was $0.34/share for the first nine months of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the increase in revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses and realized and unrealized losses on commodity contracts


- Adjusted EBITDA(1) was $44.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $31.6 million for the comparable prior year period, an increase of 41%. The increase was primarily due to the increase in revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses and realized losses on commodity contracts


- Production and operating expense per barrel averaged $8.43 per BOE in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $7.20 per BOE for the same period of 2025, an increase of 17%. The increase was primarily due to higher severance taxes due to higher prices, workover costs on a non-operated well and higher chemical and water hauling costs


- Average netback from operations(2) for the first nine months of 2026 was $41.85 per BOE, an increase of 27% from the prior year period due to higher prices. Netback including commodity contracts(2) for the first nine months of 2026 was $39.79 per BOE which was 21% higher than the comparable prior year period

First Nine Months of 2026 versus First Nine Months of 2025


Oil and gas gross revenues totaled $76.2 million in the first nine months of 2026 versus $53.7 million in the first nine months of 2025, an increase of 42%. Oil revenues were $68.7 million in the first nine months of 2026 versus $46.5 million in the same period of 2025, an increase of 48%, as average oil prices increased by 26% and production increased by 17%. Natural gas revenues decreased by 9% due to an average natural gas price decrease of 7% and a 2% decrease in natural gas production. NGL revenue increased by 12% due to an increase in NGL production of 18% partially offset by a 5% price decrease.


Average production per day for the first nine months of 2026 increased 15% to 4,412 BOEPD from the prior year comparable period. The increase is due to production from the wells that were drilled and completed in the fourth quarter of 2025.


Production and operating expenses increased to $8.9 million or 37% in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the prior year period. Production and operating expense per barrel averaged $8.43 per BOE in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $7.20 per BOE for the same period of 2025, an increase of 17%. The increase was primarily due to higher severance taxes due to higher prices, workover costs on a non-operated well, higher water hauling costs in the first half of the year and higher chemical costs in 2026.


General and administrative expenses were $4.5 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $4.1 million in the comparable prior year period due to an increase in consulting and legal costs.


Finance expense increased by $6.5 million in the first nine months of 2026 due to a $3.2 million unrealized loss on commodity contracts and a $2.5 million realized losses on commodity contracts in 2026.

**PRODUCT TYPE DISCLOSURE**


This news release includes references to sales volumes of “oil”, “natural gas”, and “barrels of oil equivalent” or “BOEs”. “Oil” refers to light crude oil and medium crude oil combined, and “natural gas” refers to shale gas, in each case as defined by NI 51-101. Production from our wells, primarily disclosed in this news release in BOEs, consists of mainly oil and associated wet gas. The wet gas is delivered via gathering system and then pipelines to processing plants where it is treated and sold as natural gas and NGLs.


**CAUTIONARY STATEMENTS**


In this news release and the Company’s other public disclosure:


(a)


The Company’s natural gas production is reported in thousands of cubic feet (“Mcfs”). The Company also uses references to barrels (“Bbls”) and barrels of oil equivalent (“BOEs”) to reflect natural gas liquids and oil production and sales. BOEs may be misleading, particularly if used in isolation. A BOE conversion ratio of 6 Mcf:1 Bbl is based on an energy equivalency conversion method primarily applicable at the burner tip and does not represent a value equivalency at the wellhead. Given that the value ratio based on the current price of crude oil as compared to natural gas is significantly different from the energy equivalency of 6:1, utilizing a conversion on a 6:1 basis may be misleading as an indication of value.


(b)


Discounted and undiscounted net present value of future net revenues attributable to reserves do not represent fair market value.


(c)


Possible reserves are those additional reserves that are less certain to be recovered than probable reserves. There is a 10% probability that the quantities actually recovered will equal or exceed the sum of proved plus probable plus possible reserves.


(d)


The Company discloses peak and 30-day initial production rates and other short-term production rates. Readers are cautioned that such production rates are preliminary in nature and are not necessarily indicative of long-term performance or of ultimate recovery.
